prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map captures a large open grassy field receding from bright foreground grass (1–5 m away) toward a dark treeline and distant city skyline over 100 m away, with the sky rendered completely black. Across frames 1 to 3 and 5, three standing people appear as small vertical silhouettes spaced roughly 15–25 m apart from left to right along the field: the leftmost person (in a white top) is roughly 15–20 m from the camera wearer, the middle person (in blue) is about 30–35 m away, and the rightmost person is roughly 45–55 m away, so none are within arm's reach of the camera wearer or each other. In frame 4, the camera wearer pitches upward toward the sky as a flying disc (frisbee) approaches overhead at roughly 2–4 m distance, before pitching back down to the field in frame 5 where the foreground grass on the right appears brightest and closest. The depth map makes the continuous ground-plane gradient, camera tilt, and the mid-air disc's silhouette in frame 4 stand out more clearly than against the bright clouds in RGB. However, it is unreliable for the airborne disc in frame 4—assigning it a relatively dark, mid-range intensity despite its close proximity against the sky—and fails to resolve the fine limb geometry of the distant people.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete foreground entities against a black background, detecting three people spaced left-to-right across the field (at roughly 15–20 m, 30–35 m, and 45–55 m from the camera wearer) in frames 1–3, a distant background car (>80 m away to the left) in frames 1–2, and the airborne disc in frame 4. In frame 1, the leftmost person (~18 m away) holds a white disc within their arm's reach and faces toward the camera wearer; by frame 3, as the camera tilts up, that person is partially cropped at the bottom edge of the frame with their arms raised after releasing the disc. In frame 4, as the disc flies overhead within a few metres of the camera wearer, the map segments it mid-air, and in frame 5, as the camera turns and tilts down to the right, a brown mask at the bottom-left edge marks part of the camera wearer's own body or arm within immediate reach (<0.5 m) while only two distant people remain segmented on the field. This map highlights tiny distant figures (the rightmost person at ~50 m and the parked car) that are very hard to spot in the RGB image alone. However, it is unreliable in misclassifying the flying frisbee as a 'kite' in frame 4, missing the leftmost person near the left frame border in frame 5, and omitting the parked car in frame 3.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all 5 frames, failing to detect any body or hand skeletons for either the distant people on the field or the camera wearer. From the RGB context, three people stand in the open field roughly 15–55 m away from the camera wearer and 15–25 m apart from each other, with the leftmost person (~15–20 m away) facing the camera wearer, holding a frisbee within arm's reach in frames 1–2, and raising both arms to throw it toward the camera wearer in frame 3. In frame 4, the camera wearer tilts their head steeply upward to track the approaching disc a few metres overhead, and in frame 5 tilts back down and turns slightly right, bringing part of the wearer's own lower-left torso/arm into the bottom-left corner within arm's reach (<0.5 m) while the leftmost person on the field is near the far-left edge. Unlike the RGB image—where the leftmost person's throwing posture and facing direction can still be discerned—the pose map provides no additional spatial information. It is entirely unreliable at these medium-to-far distances (15+ m), where subjects occupy only a few pixels, as well as for the heavily cropped, close-up view of the camera wearer's own body part in frame 5.
